mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.25%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 9.0% for two consecutive months signals economic distress, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 9.0% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicate a weakening demand cycle, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative returns: 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 95.0) and rising capacity utilization, the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to recessionary supply shocks, producing negative returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is below 95.0.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the CPI (CPIAUCSL > 225.0) signals accelerating inflation, prompting the Fed to tighten policy and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 225.0.

mechanism_narrative: A rising labor force participation (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly) indicates improving economic conditions, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.5% monthly.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in consumer spending (RSAFS) and industrial production (INDPRO) signals a broad-based economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in RSAFS and INDPRO fails to predict negative returns: 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 94.0) indicates weakening supply capacity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is below 94.0.
